summary: Created scripts/build-skills.js using the @mistralys/persona-builder programmatic API with a custom TargetRegistry containing vscode-skill and claude-skill targets.

Script imports the CJS distribution of persona-builder via createRequire (parallel to build-personas.js pattern) and calls build() directly — the CLI binary cannot be used because it doesn't support custom registry injection.
vscode-skill target: name + description + conditional argument-hint frontmatter (omits context/agent for VS Code compatibility).
claude-skill target: name + description + conditional context + conditional agent frontmatter (produces context: fork, agent: persona-curator for the insights-audit-persona skill).
Script clears output directories before building, skips writes in --check/--dry-run mode, and exits non-zero on build failure.

All 5 acceptance criteria verified: build succeeds (exit 0), VS Code output omits context/agent/argument-hint, Claude output includes context: fork and agent: persona-curator, --check exits 0 with 0 files written, both files contain rendered Audit mode body.

comments.note: The Claude Code skill frontmatter template (recommended pattern from building-skills.md) produces a blank line between 'context: fork' and 'agent: persona-curator' due to the persona-builder's conditional resolver surrounding truthy blocks with \n delimiters. This is harmless — YAML parsers tolerate blank lines in mappings — but worth noting. The pattern matches the library's own documentation example.
scripts/build-skills.js is ESM-only (import.meta.dirname). If a CJS consumer ever needs to run this script it would require a wrapper. No concern for current usage (workspace root has type: module).

summary: scripts/build-skills.js passes all Review Dimensions — clean, well-structured, follows established codebase patterns throughout.

Maintainability: 150 lines, descriptive variable names (ROOT, LIB, SKILLS, DIST, CHECK, STRICT), frontmatter templates defined as module-level constants, inline comments explain each design decision. No unnecessary complexity.

Best Practices: createRequire + index.cjs mirrors build-personas.js pattern exactly. path.join used throughout (cross-platform). Pre-build cleanup filters .md files only and is correctly guarded by if(!CHECK). Top-level await is valid in ESM context (workspace type:module). process.exit(1) on error is appropriate for a build script.
Performance: No concerns for a build script. Synchronous directory cleanup is standard.

Future Context: Separation from build-personas.js (independent registry, independent output dirs) is well-justified — adding future skill targets requires only skillRegistry.register(). The custom TargetRegistry pattern is clean and extensible.

Output verified live: VS Code file contains name+description only (no context/agent/argument-hint). Claude file contains name+description+context:fork+agent:persona-curator with a harmless blank line (valid YAML confirmed by QA).
No blocking issues, no fix-forward candidates identified.

comments.note: The pre-build cleanup only removes .md files at the top level of each output directory. If a future skill were to produce subdirectories (not possible with the current flat structure), stale files in those subdirectories would linger. No action required now, but worth keeping in mind if the skill structure ever becomes nested.
